newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends firmer ahead of U.S. holiday.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends firmer ahead of U.S. holiday.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended slightly higher Friday, as locals scrambled to cover short positions ahead of the three-day holiday weekend, dealers said.
The CSCE will be closed Monday for the U.S. Labor Day holiday.

The Benchmark December concract ended up 1.20 cents a lb, to 118.25 cents, after ranging between 118.75 and 116.00. Spot September ended 0.25 cent firmer, at 128.35, while the remaining months finished flat to 0.90 higher.
Technically, traders pegged resistance at 120 in the December contract, while support was seen at 115.

Although September's open interest continued to decline, it remained relatively high Thursday at 1,279 lots -- the equivalent of nearly 320,000 60-kg bags -- compared to the 39,313 60-kg bags of certified coffee stocks stored in CSCE warehouses.
The CSCE weekly certified stock report, usually released late Monday, will be come out after the close of business on Tuesday due to the Labor Day holiday.
Dealers await the CFTC Commitment of Traders report due after the close of business Friday. They said a substantial increase in non-commercial long positions could weigh on the market.
"I think the market may be a little overbought," one trader said.
Volume was light, at an estimated 3,906 lots.
